Independently verified this is a correct, working restoration of the visible keyboard-focus ring, not merely a plausible-looking class-string edit. InlineTitle.tsx: outline-none deleted from the input's own className (confirmed by directly reading the current file), so the pre-existing global :focus-visible base rule in styles.css (unchanged @layer base block: outline 2px solid var(--color-accent), outline-offset 2px, box-shadow 0 0 0 4px var(--color-bg)) now applies directly and completely - no gap. CaptureDeck.tsx: the <input> itself keeps outline-none (a <form> is not natively focusable, so ringing the input directly would need InlineTitle's exact fix); instead the implementer rings the parent <form> via has-[input:focus-visible]:outline-2/outline-accent/outline-offset-2/[box-shadow:...]. This reviewer did not accept Tailwind utility semantics on faith: read the actual compiled dist/client CSS directly. Found '.has-[input:focus-visible]:outline-2:has(:is(input:focus-visible)){outline-style:var(--tw-outline-style);outline-width:2px}' plus a project-wide '@property --tw-outline-style{syntax:"*";inherits:false;initial-value:solid}' registration; since the <form> carries no outline-none/outline-hidden class of its own, --tw-outline-style resolves to its registered initial value 'solid' on that element, so the conditional ring genuinely paints solid amber at 2px with a 2px offset plus the halo box-shadow when the nested input is keyboard-focused - functionally identical to the base :focus-visible recipe, just re-expressed as four composable utilities gated by :has() on the ancestor because the input, not the form, is what actually receives focus. A K=5 sub-agent pass (code-reviewer-semantic, dispatched via Task) initially flagged this exact mechanism as R-COH-TASK-CONTRADICTION, claiming outline-style is never set on the form and only the box-shadow halo would render, reproducing the original bug; this reviewer independently falsified that claim against the compiled CSS evidence above rather than propagating an untested Tailwind v4 semantics guess, and recorded R-COH-TASK-CONTRADICTION as passed with the sub-agent's concern and this refutation both preserved for audit (see that row). Minor non-blocking trade-off noted: has-[input:focus-visible]:[box-shadow:...] has higher CSS specificity (0,2,1) than .shadow-field (0,1,0) within the same Tailwind utilities cascade layer, so the deck's inset field shadow is replaced, not composed, by the halo while focused - a reasonable, common trade-off, not a functional defect. AC-A9 holds: outline-accent and var(--color-bg) are token references, never literal colours, and no style={} object was introduced. No new bugs, no security gaps, no business-rule regression from this 3-file delta; both deviations from the plan's literal Task 4/Task 5 class strings are required, in-scope corrections of the exact defect the main session's mandatory guidelines section-4.5 check found, and none of the plan's own VALIDATE greps for either file assert the removed/added substrings, so no gate silently broke.
